records.finding: The closing paragraph of the export-adapter section asserted that 'every exporter here rejects a family it does not recognise rather than guessing a kind for it' and that 'Each adapter pins this in its own unit tests'. 'here' quantifies over the export-adapter table, whose fourth row is adapters/export/gcp. This branch deleted gcp's monitoring.go (labelsFor / unknownFamilyError) and monitoring_test.go (TestMetricExportRejections, subtest 'unknown family surfaces rather than being dropped'), so gcp's ExportMetrics now accepts any family and discards it, and no gcp test pins family recognition. cloudwatch, otlp and prometheus still reject. The sentence over-claimed by exactly one adapter after the diff.

Each adapter pins this in its own unit tests'. Contradicting artifact, adapters/export/gcp/gcp.go:91-93: `func (e *Exporter) ExportMetrics(context.Context, []emit.MetricPoint) error { return nil }` — no family check, no error.
records.reason: Fixed in 53d0b6e by scoping the claim to the exporters that ship metrics and naming gcp as an exception with its reason ('declaring Metrics: false, it ships no metric point of any family, so there is no kind for it to guess at'). Restoring a family table in gcp was rejected as the fix: it would be validation logic in an exporter that ships nothing to validate, and the tracked item's scope is to delete everything serving the metrics path. The scoped re-reviewer verdicted 'addressed' and verified every sentence of the new paragraph against the tree — exactly three table rows declare Metrics:true (otlp/otlp.go:201, prometheus/prometheus.go:154, cloudwatch/cloudwatch.go:114), all three reject in code (otlp/metrics.go:55, prometheus/prometheus.go:188, cloudwatch/cloudwatch.go:155 and emf.go:81), all three pin it in their own package unit tests (otlp/pipeline_test.go:195, prometheus_test.go:98, cloudwatch_test.go:72), and testkit/conformance's Check() runs no family check. new_issues: [].

records.finding: Raised by the cross-examiner as a cross-cutting note rather than by the reviewer. Section 6.2 states the unrecognised-family invariant as an unscoped MUST — 'An exporter handed a metric point whose family it does not recognise MUST surface an error for that batch. It MUST NOT drop the point' — and the port checklist repeats it. As literally written that binds adapters/export/gcp, which after this diff recognises no families at all and neither errors nor keeps the point. Until it is scoped, portability.md and the reworded docs/adapters.md state one standard at two widths.

records.reason: Raised by the cross-examiner as a cross-cutting NOTE, not filed as a finding against this diff — it explicitly declined to raise one, being an examiner rather than a filer. PARKED on tracked item workspace-82c (P2). docs/portability.md was explicitly out of scope for this branch (a concurrently-edited path), so it could not be fixed here. The bead records the correct fix and rules out the wrong one: scope 6.2 and its checklist line to exporters declaring Metrics:true, matching what testkit/conformance's metricHonesty already encodes ('An incapable signal may return an error (signalling a drop) — that is honest. What it must never do is silently deliver'). Making gcp error instead would have emit.Std.Flush treat every flush as a failed metric batch — a warning logged and biz_dropped_events_total re-credited forever, and a non-nil error returned from every Flush, for a signal the exporter never claimed. The tension is real, tracked, and out of scope rather than resolved.
